text: Some voices carry further than they should. The lantern is lit.
picture: The Storyteller stands in deep mist, his boots in shadow, holding a red lantern low. Far behind him, a single upstairs window of a lonely house glows yellow. An eerie, watchful stillness.

text: My daughter Lily is four. She sleeps with the baby monitor on.
picture: A wide view of Lily's small, calm bedroom. Lily is asleep under a star-patterned duvet. A soft star night-light glows. The baby monitor sits on the bedside table, its small red light a tiny dot.

text: Last night, at twelve past three, it crackled. Lily was whispering.
picture: A tight focus on Mara’s face in bed, awake and listening, eyes wide. The baby monitor receiver beside her glows with red sound-level lights. Her expression is frozen mid-breath.
A close-up of Lily asleep in bed, her lips barely moving in a whisper. Her eyes are shut. The soft star night‑light glows on her face, her expression troubled.

text: Then another voice. Low. Patient. "Mummy is asleep."
picture: Lily’s dark room. Lily sleeps facing the wall. The baby monitor transmitter sits on her nightstand, a single red light pulsing faintly. Deep shadows fill the corner.

text: I ran. Her door was shut. Her night-light was off. I had left it on.
picture: A wide, high-angle view of a dark upstairs landing lit by one failing bulb. Mara stands at Lily's closed bedroom door, her hand on the handle. No light escapes from under the door. Deep shadows pool.

text: Lily was asleep, facing the wall. Nobody else.
picture: Through the open doorway, Lily's bedroom in darkness. A small mound in bed, Lily asleep facing the wall in her starry pyjamas. Her night-light is dead. Deep, empty shadows fill the corners of the room. The grey pre-dawn light from one window barely touches the floor.

text: I sat on her floor until dawn, the monitor in my lap. At twenty to five, it crackled again. Lily hadn't moved.
picture: Mara sits exhausted against the wall on Lily's floor, the baby monitor receiver in her lap. A weak grey dawn light silhouettes a foggy window behind her. Lily sleeps unmoving in her bed beside Mara. A small red light glows in the darkness of the receiver.

text: Then the voice came, so close it touched the microphone. "Mummy's awake now."
picture: A tight shot of Mara frozen on the floor, face a mask of terror, staring down at the receiver in her lap. Its red light glows brightly in the dark room.

text: Lily is five now. She still won't sleep without the monitor. She says he likes to listen.
picture: The Storyteller stands in the hollow, his expression eerie and knowing as he lowers his red lantern. Far behind him, on the silhouette of their house, a single small upstairs window glows faintly. Inside that window, a tiny, distinct red light winks from the darkness.
